# Phase 0 closure matrix

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/closure_matrix.py from docs/closure-matrix.json. Do not edit; run the script. -->

**What "closed" means** (plan section 2). A row or gap is closed only when all of these hold:

1. Built and merged.
2. An enforcing caller exists and is ON by default.
3. A both-provider (Claude and Codex) proof exists, with a negative control.
4. Installed live.
5. Reason codes, trace, runbook entry and measurement exist.
6. Limits are documented.

The integrity gate (gap1) stays opt-in. It is the documented exception, closed by
[`INTEGRITY-GATE.md`](INTEGRITY-GATE.md), is not installed here, and gets no second enforcement route.

Phase 0 and Phase 7 are cross-cutting. Phase 7 is the live cutover and closure acceptance for every row.

## Gaps

| id | gap | phase or exception | acceptance test | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gap1 | external trust enforcement | EXCEPTION: closed by the existing opt-in integrity gate (docs/INTEGRITY-GATE.md). It stays opt-in, is not installed here, and gets no second enforcement route. | A test fails if any enforcement hook or route is registered outside the existing integrity-gate installer (scripts/integrity-gate/setup.py); the gate stays opt-in (inactive without integrity_review.machine_user) and is not installed here. | open |
| gap2 | capability-based tools | Phase 3 | Per-role capability MCP servers (scripts/capability.py + capabilities/profiles.json) expose only profile tools; a test shows a reviewer session lists no shell tool, a wrong-role tool call and an arbitrary command are denied, in both providers; the profile file and the servers cannot drift. | open |
| gap3 | HITL / action authority | Phase 3 | A test shows the authority grant command and receipts bound to repository+ref+SHA gate gh pr merge and git push to main by default: a stale SHA, a replayed receipt and a self-minted receipt are rejected, in both providers. | open |
| gap4 | dynamic task-specific context | Phase 6 | A test shows controller-supplied mandatory context and budgets are rendered into the dispatch envelope and removing a trigger keyword cannot omit a required skill or check; a worker prompt lacking the mandatory context is rejected, in both providers. | open |
| gap5 | typed memory (Muninn) | Phase 5 | A test shows the Muninn adapter is authoritative by default: records round-trip through the typed schema after a restart, an untyped record is rejected, and a missing or refusing Muninn fails with a reason code and never falls back silently to Markdown. | open |
